newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to detail windfall tax if wins election.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to detail windfall tax if wins election.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Monday it would detail its plans for a windfall tax on privatised utilities -- and possibly other privatised companies -- only if it came to power at the next election.

A spokesman for Labour's Gordon Brown said the finance spokesman planned to make no further statement on the proposed tax -- which newspapers say could raise 10 billion stg -- at key speech at 1445 GMT.
"He (Brown) has said all he's got to say on the windfall tax," the spokesman told Reuters: "He will today confirm (only) that there will be a windfall levy on privatised utilities."
Asked when the party would detail its windfall tax plans, the spokesman said only: "In Gordon Brown's first Budget."

The spokesman again dismissed as "pure speculation" a newspaper report the party was planning to raise 10 billion stg -- double the 3-5 billion stg estimated so far -- from a tax on the profits of groups such as electricity, water, gas, telecoms, airline firms and the old airports authority BAA.

"Sunday papers have a habit of plucking figures out of the air," he said: "Gordon Brown will not pluck the figure out of the air...he will consult the regulators and the privatised utility bosses before announcing any figure."
Brown said earlier that the party's public spending programme would require no new spending commitments other than those financed by the windfall tax.
He made no further reference to the proposed tax -- or to which companies such a tax would apply.
